To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the annealing behaviour in the case of arsenic implantation in silicon is strongly affected by the heating rates employed.

the density and depth distributions of residual damage in As-implanted Si wafers annealed at 850 degrees C for 5 s are markedly influenced by the heating rate of the samples (from 5 to 280 degrees C s(-1)).

the heating rate of a sample during annealing affects the annealing behaviour, which is interpreted in terms of the trapping efficiency of self-interstitial atoms during regrowth of an amorphised layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the heating rates on the annealing process in arsenic implanted silicon.
the influence of the heating-rate on the annealing of arsenic-impurity-induced defects in silicon wafers.
the annealing of arsenic- implanted silicon wafers, employing different heating rate of the samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the annealing of ion implanted silicon is a complicated and complex process and it is very difficult, if not impossible, to give a simple and general answer to the question of the influence of the heating rates on the annealing process.
the annealing of arsenic- and phosphorus-implanted Si wafers is not a simple thermal process but is strongly influenced by the kinetics of the regrowth process.
the heating rate has to be considered as a critical parameter when studying the annealing behaviour in ion implanted semiconductors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heating rate has a strong impact on the regrowth behaviour of the arsenic-implantation-induced amorphous layer.
the heating rate is a very important factor for the annealing of arsenic-Implanted silicon.
the regrowth rate has to be taken into account in order to explain the influence of the heating ramp on the annealing of arsenic-impurities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heating rate can be used to tailor the defect structure and hence the properties of arsenic-impurity layers in silicon.
the annealing process is a dynamic process that depends on many parameters, and that it is not a static process that can be controlled by the temperature alone.
the regrowth rate of the amorphous layer is a key factor to consider when annealing arsenic-implants in silicon.
